title: Handshakes at a party
question: If everyone at a party shakes hands with everyone else once, is the number of handshakes always n(n-1)/2?
plain_restatement: At a party of p people where each pair shakes hands once, the number of handshakes is p times (p minus 1), divided by 2.
fidelity_note: Checks parties of up to 3,000 people by counting every pair.
